content.title: Bug: removeAllBlockagesForIssue has inverted counterpart filter
content.description:
In dependency-manager.ts line 200, the filter condition for removing counterpart entries from the blocks map is incorrect.

## Bug Location
`src/core/dependency-manager.ts` line 200

## Current (Buggy) Code
```typescript
const filtered = blockerBlocks.filter(
  (e) => !(e.blockerId === issueId && e.blockedId === entry.blockedId),
);
```

## Expected Code
```typescript
const filtered = blockerBlocks.filter(
  (e) => !(e.blockerId === entry.blockerId && e.blockedId === entry.blockedId),
);
```

## Explanation
When iterating `blockedBy[issueId]` entries, `issueId` is the BLOCKED issue and `entry.blockerId` is the blocker. The counterpart entries in `blocks[entry.blockerId]` have `blockerId: entry.blockerId` and `blockedId: issueId`. The filter should check `e.blockerId === entry.blockerId`, but instead it checks `e.blockerId === issueId` (the blocked issue ID), which never matches for the counterpart.

This causes counterpart entries in the `blocks` map to NOT be cleaned up when deleting a blocked issue. Only the second part of the function (cleaning up `blockedBy` counterparts when the issue is a blocker) is correct.

## Impact
- `removeAllBlockagesForIssue` does not clean up counterpart entries in the blocks map
- `tracker.issueDelete()` leaves stale blockage references behind
- Found during validation of delete command (mps4uwcsqx)

content.content: Created child implementation task mpscw71ria assigned to library-developer. The bug is a one-line fix with a clear description — the filter in removeAllBlockagesForIssue uses issueId instead of entry.blockerId when cleaning up counterpart entries from the blocks map. Will close this parent once the child is done.
